card.title: FORTRESS DARWIN
card.text: Fortress Darwin was a vital Allied outpost during WWII.
card.flavorText: By 1942, Darwin had changed from a small northern town into a crowded Allied base. Its pre-war population was only about 5,800, but its harbour, airfields, roads, and fuel stores made it vital for operations toward Timor, Java, and the Philippines. The defence works grew around the peninsula. East Point guarded the sea approaches with 6-inch coastal guns, while anti-aircraft positions covered Fannie Bay, East Arm, and the airfields. A 6 km boom net stretched across Darwin Harbour to block submarines and small surface craft. The fortress was still unfinished when Japan struck in 1942. Darwin had 18 heavy anti-aircraft guns, limited fighter strength, and no working radar warning system. On 19 February, carrier-based aircraft and land-based bombers hit the harbour, town, and airfields. MV Neptuna exploded at Stokes Hill Wharf, USS Peary was sunk, and RAAF Darwin was badly damaged. The raids exposed Darwin’s weakness, but they also forced a larger Allied air build-up across northern Australia.
